To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

insulin-induced hypogycemia (IIH), a physiological stimulus, inhibits luteinizing hormone (LH) secretion in unrestrained, intact female rhesus macaques during their follicular phase of their menstrual cycle.
Insulin-induced hypoglycaemia (IIH), a stressor, inhibits luteinizing hormone (LH) release in intact female macaques and that this effect is independent of vasopressine and opioidergic mechanisms.

hypoglycemic inhibition of LH secretion in female macaques is not due to direct effects of glucose on the GnRH neurone and that vasopressin or endogenous opioids are not sufficient to account for the inhibition of LH release induced by hypoglucemia.
